issues.legal_issue: Statutory authority to recover public dues by arrest and detention of a defaulter is constitutionally valid.
material_facts: The petitioners owed dues to a bank that were recoverable through statutory recovery proceedings.
The petitioners challenged the constitutional validity of provisions authorising arrest and detention to recover those dues, fearing they would be arrested and detained.
The Court had upheld the constitutional validity of the challenged provisions in an earlier judgment delivered the same day.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the constitutional challenge and dismissed the petitions, leaving the revenue authorities free to recover the dues according to law and in light of the earlier judgment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its holding in Ram Narayan Agarwal v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Writ Petitions Nos. 1110 of 1980 and connected matters, decided the same day, that Section 279(1)(b) and Section 281 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, which authorise recovery of arrears by arrest and detention, are constitutionally valid. The dues were recoverable under the U.P. Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1972, read with Section 279 of the 1950 Act.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenges_arrest_fo: A person brought a constitutional writ challenging statutory authority to arrest and detain a defaulter to recover dues.
predicates.dues_are_recoverable_through_statutory_p: The dues at issue were recoverable through statutory proceedings conducted by revenue authorities.
predicates.precedent_upheld_same_recovery_authority: The Court had already upheld the constitutional validity of the same recovery authority in an earlier decision.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ challenges arrest for recovery of statutory dues, the dues are recoverable through statutory proceedings, and an earlier decision upheld the same recovery authority, the challenged recovery authority is constitutional.
